His younger full brothers Murong Ren, general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Murong Zhao, general who extends martial power, were both favored by Hui, which also displeased Huang.
repairs.sourceQuote: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
repairs.reason: Preserve the flashback 初, long-standing jealousy 素, all three abbreviated offices 建威/征虜/廣武 and younger maternal brothers 母弟; names must remain distinguishable from offices.

repairs.after: At first, Huang's elder brother by a concubine, Han, the general who establishes might, was brave in warfare and had heroic talent; Huang had long been jealous of him. His younger brothers by the same mother, Ren, the general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Zhao, the general who extends martial power, both enjoyed Hui's favor; Huang was also displeased with them.

repairs.reason: Preserve the flashback 初, long-standing jealousy 素, all three abbreviated offices 建威/征虜/廣武 and younger maternal brothers 母弟; names must remain distinguishable from offices.

repairs.after: Huang dispatched his younger brother Murong You, general who establishes martial power, Marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against Ren.

repairs.reason: Preserve the abbreviated office 建武 attached to You, the younger-brother relation 弟 and inclusive 等; 建武 here is an office, not a reign date.

repairs.before: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
repairs.after: Huang sent his younger brother You, the general who establishes martial power, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
repairs.sourceQuote: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
repairs.reason: Preserve the abbreviated office 建武 attached to You, the younger-brother relation 弟 and inclusive 等; 建武 here is an office, not a reign date.

context.zh: 慕容皝，字元真，廆第三子也。
context.idiomatic: Murong Huang, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhen, was Murong Hui’s third son.
context.literal: Murong Huang, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was the third son of Murong Hui.

context.zh: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
context.idiomatic: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
context.literal: Dragon face and “plaque” teeth; body height seven chi eight cun.

context.zh: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
context.idiomatic: He was bold, resourceful, devoted to the classics, and adept at reading the stars.
context.literal: Heroic and resolute, abundant in stratagem; esteemed classical learning; skilled in astronomy.

context.zh: 廆為遼東公，立為世子。
context.idiomatic: When Murong Hui was named duke of Liaodong, Huang was made his heir.
context.literal: When Hui became Duke of Liaodong, he was established as heir apparent.

context.zh: 建武初，拜為冠軍將軍、左賢王，封望平侯，率眾征討，累有功。
context.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era he was named general who champions the army and left worthy prince, created marquis of Wangping, and led troops on several successful expeditions.
context.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, appointed General Who Champions the Army, Left Worthy Prince, enfeoffed Marquis of Wangping; led host in campaigns; repeatedly had merit.

context.zh: 太甯末，拜平北將軍，進封朝鮮公。
context.idiomatic: Late in the Taining era he became general who pacifies the north and was promoted to duke of Chaoxian.
context.literal: At the end of Taining, appointed General Who Pacifies the North; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Chaoxian.

context.zh: 廆卒，嗣位，以平北將軍行平州刺史，督攝部內。
context.idiomatic: When Hui died he succeeded him, serving as general who pacifies the north and acting governor of Pingzhou with authority over the whole command.
context.literal: When Hui died, he succeeded the position; as general who pacifies the north acted as governor of Ping Province, supervising and holding the interior of the command.

context.zh: 尋而宇文乞得龜為其別部逸豆歸所逐，奔死於外，皝率騎討之，逸豆歸懼而請和，遂築榆陰、安晉二城而還。
context.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
context.literal: Soon Yuwen Qidegui was by his separate division Yidougui expelled, fled and died outside; Huang led cavalry to campaign against him; Yidougui feared and requested peace; thereupon built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and returned.

context.zh: 初，皝庶兄建威翰驍武有雄才，素為皝所忌，母弟征虜仁、廣武昭並有寵於廆，皝亦不平之。
context.idiomatic: His elder half-brother Murong Han, who held the title general who establishes might, was a brilliant warrior whom Huang resented, while his full brothers Murong Ren and Murong Zhao, both favored by Hui, also stirred his jealousy.
context.literal: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.

context.zh: 及廆卒，並懼不自容。
context.idiomatic: When Hui died they all feared for their lives.
context.literal: When Hui died, all feared they could not preserve themselves.

context.zh: 至此，翰出奔段遼，仁勸昭舉兵廢皝。
context.idiomatic: Murong Han fled to Duan Liao, while Murong Ren urged Murong Zhao to revolt and depose Huang.
context.literal: Reaching this point, Han fled out to Duan Liao; Ren urged Zhao to raise troops and depose Huang.

context.zh: 皝殺昭，遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆。
context.idiomatic: Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
context.literal: Huang killed Zhao, sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation, met Ren at Xiandu.

context.zh: 仁知事發，殺皝使，東歸平郭。
context.idiomatic: Ren saw his plot exposed, killed the messenger, and fled east to Pingguo.
context.literal: Ren knew the affair had broken; killed Huang’s envoy; went east to return to Pingguo.

context.zh: 皝遣其弟建武幼、司馬佟壽等討之。
context.idiomatic: Huang dispatched his brother Murong You and Marshal Tong Shou against him.
context.literal: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.

context.zh: 仁盡眾距戰，幼等大敗，皆沒於仁。
context.idiomatic: Ren threw his whole army into the fight and crushed You’s force, capturing every commander.
context.literal: Ren exhausted the host to resist battle; You and the others were greatly defeated, all lost to Ren.

context.zh: 襄平令王冰、將軍孫機以遼東叛於皝，東夷校尉封抽、護軍乙逸、遼東相韓矯、玄菟太守高詡等棄城奔還。
context.idiomatic: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, Protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned their cities and fled back.
context.literal: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned cities and fled back.

context.zh: 仁於是盡有遼左之地，自稱車騎將軍、平州刺史、遼東公。
context.idiomatic: Ren then controlled all territory east of the Liao, proclaiming himself general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Pingzhou, and duke of Liaodong.
context.literal: Ren thereupon wholly possessed the land left of the Liao, styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Ping Province, Duke of Liaodong.

context.zh: 宇文歸、段遼及鮮卑諸部並為之援，
context.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and other Xianbei chiefs backed him.
context.literal: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all became his aid.

context.zh: 咸和九年，皝遣其司馬封弈攻鮮卑木堤于白狼，揚威淑虞攻烏丸悉羅侯于平岡，皆斬之。
context.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent Marshal Feng Yi to strike the Xianbei leader Muti at Bailang and Shuyu to strike the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both enemy heads were taken.
context.literal: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent his marshal Feng Yi to attack the Xianbei Muti at Bailang, and Yangwei Shuyu to attack the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both were beheaded.

context.zh: 材官劉佩攻乙連，不克。
context.idiomatic: Engineering officer Liu Pei assaulted Yilian without success.
context.literal: Workshop officer Liu Pei attacked Yilian but could not overcome it.

context.zh: 段遼遂寇徒河，皝將張萌逆擊，敗之。
context.idiomatic: Duan Liao then invaded Tuhe, but Huang’s general Zhang Meng intercepted and routed him.
context.literal: Duan Liao thereupon raided Tuhe; Huang’s general Zhang Meng met and struck them, defeated them.

context.zh: 遼弟蘭與翰寇柳城，都尉石琮擊敗之。
context.idiomatic: Duan Lan and Murong Han attacked Liucheng until commandant Shi Cong drove them off.
context.literal: Liao’s younger brother Lan with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.

context.zh: 旬余，蘭、翰復圍柳城，皝遣甯遠慕容汗及封弈等救之。
context.idiomatic: Ten-odd days later Duan Lan and Murong Han, the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao, again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent the Ningyuan general, a different Murong Han, together with Feng Yi and others to relieve the city.
context.literal: After ten-odd days, Lan and Han again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Murong Han and Feng Yi and others to rescue it.

context.zh: 皝戒汗曰：「賊眾氣銳，難與爭鋒，宜顧萬全，慎勿輕進，必須兵集陣整，然後擊之。」
context.idiomatic: Huang warned Murong Han (the general of pacifying distance): “The foe is numerous and keen—do not trade blows rashly; wait until your force is formed, then attack.”
context.literal: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is many and their spirit sharp; hard to contend edge; ought to look to complete safety, carefully do not lightly advance; must wait until troops are gathered and lines set, then strike them.”

context.zh: 汗性驍銳，遣千餘騎為前鋒而進，封弈止之，汗不從，為蘭所敗，死者大半。
context.idiomatic: Murong Han was impetuous: he sent a thousand horse ahead as a van, ignored Feng Yi’s warning, and was routed by Duan Lan with heavy losses.
context.literal: Han’s nature was fierce and sharp; dispatched over a thousand cavalry as vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him; Han did not follow; was defeated by Lan; dead were more than half.

context.zh: 蘭復攻柳城，為飛梯、地道，圍守二旬，石琮躬勒將士出擊，敗之，斬首千五百級，蘭乃遁歸。
context.idiomatic: Duan Lan renewed the siege with ladders and tunnels, but after twenty days Shi Cong sallied forth, killed fifteen hundred men, and forced Lan to withdraw.
context.literal: Lan again attacked Liucheng, made flying ladders and tunnels, besieged and guarded twenty days; Shi Cong personally led officers and soldiers out to strike, defeated them, beheaded fifteen hundred grades; Lan then fled and returned.

context.zh: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
context.idiomatic: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
context.literal: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
